newsitem.title: UK: European firms still wary of Internet.
newsitem.headline: European firms still wary of Internet.

text.p: By Neil Winton, Science and Technology Correspondent

The Internet is seen by many European companies as an overworked buzzword, believing this network of computers is still a long way from acceptance as a key business tool, according to a survey published on Thursday.

"European companies recognised the importance of the Internet, but many believe that serious challenges remain before it can achieve its full potential in driving corporate computing environments," said a survey by International Data Group, a U.S. information technology consultancy and publisher.

Many big corporations, especially in the U.S., believe that by the end of the century, business transacted will be massive "on-line" on the Internet -- the worldwide network of personal computers linked by telephone lines first developed in the 1960s by the U.S. military, mastered by academics and popularised with the advent of cheap personal computer in the 1980s.
But some are suspicious of the hyperbole surrounding the Internet which is very much a minority pursuit amongst Europeans and European companies.
Of the world's major industrial nations, the U.S. followed by Britain are leading users of Internet technology but other Europeans lag far behind.

"European corporate expectations of the Internet vary by geographical market, with 39 per cent of British, 20 percent of German and 13 percent of French companies who took part in the study currently using the Internet," the study said.
"In the next 12 months, an additional 20 percent, 25 percent and 15 percent respectively are planning to begin using it."
"American companies lead in Internet usage closely followed by the U.K. French companies were the slowest to take advantage of this new technology," the study said.
The survey, among 1,900 companies in Britain, France, Germany, the U.S., and Japan, showed that the main driver for Internet use was marketing of products and services.
Rana Mainee, director of IDG consulting services, said companies find the Internet, which he said seamlessly integrated computing and communications for companies, is becoming an indispensible tool.
"The Internet makes for a closely knit community within the company and allows a company to become closer to its objective, closer to its focus," Mainee said.
Industrial sectors which will lead the way with Internet use are finance, insurance, manufacturing, wholesale distribution and retail, particularly direct selling.

"We are not saying that these Internet investments are going to be hugely profitable for these companies; it's really too early to say that. It is another great tool to get you closer to your objectives," Mainee said.
In the survey, companies saw the Internet as an evolution rather than a revolution.
But Mainee said this could be a dangerous underestimate.

"This is definitely a revolution because of what it allows companies to do. It's the best tool that you've got; allows you to integrate your business focus with your technology investment, and even create new revenue streams," Mainee said.
